messages.subject: orderMarkers
parts:
Hello everyone

I am relative new in using rQTL and I would like to ask you something.

I have 500 markers which I already know that belong in the same linkage group.

The only thing that I want to estimate is their order. 

I have prepared my rqtl according to the tutorial and I have placed them in the same linkage group.

data <- orderMarkers(data, chr=10, use.ripple=TRUE, error.prob=0,005)

The above command is enough or I have to calculate before "recombination fractions" and  'LOD".

Thank a  lot for your time

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] orderMarkers
parts:
That's enough. orderMarkers doesn't use pairwise recombination fractions.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: orderMarkers
parts:
orderMarkers will call switch.order, which does re-estimate the inter-marker distances, so there's no need to call est.map.
But it doesn't hurt to do so; it should be quick.

https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/map_construction.R#L178-L180

karl

Dear Dr. Karl Broman 

Thank  you a lot for you useful and accurate answers.

I would like to come with one more question.

I have my markers ordered and placed as I want but the size in cM of my linkage group seems huge. 

It should be like 200cM but it is 1400cM

any suggestions how I could deal with this expansion,

So far I have tried a lot to reduce the missing values in my data and genotypes errors.

Thank you a lot for your time

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] orderMarkers
parts:
It's probably the case that you have a couple of badly behaved markers, or markers that don't belong on that linkage group.
I would look at a plot of the map, and look for markers surrounded by big gaps.

karl
